html:
SMTO-TSK-0019 — This run is already stopping or finished

GUID: 2590ba6d-21c1-4ee4-beaa-49f9259208cc
Slug: stop-already-committed
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • You tried to change how this run should stop, but it is already stopping or has ended. Its stop setting is kept as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page and look at the run's latest reply to see whether it shows Stopping…, Stopped or finished. This confirms the run already ended, so there is nothing left for the stop setting to change.
  2. Open Agent Checks, choose This conversation or Global, and change Stop behavior there. These choices apply your preferred way of stopping to tasks you start next.

What success looks like

  • The stop setting saves for the conversation or Global, and the next task uses it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to change the finished run's stop setting; it records what already happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run-scoped Stop policy edit was rejected because the run already has a committed cancellation or has reached a terminal status.

What this means

  • A Stop-policy edit encounters an already committed cancellation or terminal run. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • A Stop-policy edit encounters an already committed cancellation or terminal run.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the durable cancellation and terminal status; this boundary rejects a policy edit rather than undoing a Stop.

How to fix it

  • Stop-policy edits at run scope are refused once a native_cancellations row exists or the run status is terminal. Reload the run to see its settled state and recorded Stop decision; set a different Stop policy at conversation or global scope for future tasks.
  • Refresh the run's status and retained Stop decision; configure any different policy for eligible future work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The retained Stop decision remains consistent with the run's settled state.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
